title: AdCP Trust Record
description: PROPOSAL (RFC #7809) — not part of the published protocol. An organization's AdCP trust record, hosted at /.well-known/adcp-trust.json on the organization's own host. Carries the trust facts that brand.json carries today: the agents the organization runs and their signing keys, the demand-side grants the organization issues, and the organization's acknowledgements of supply-side grants it has received. Identity (names, logos, colors, owned properties, brand family) stays in brand.json; publisher inventory grants stay in adagents.json. The organization this record speaks for is the host that serves /.well-known/adcp-trust.json — never a value inside the document. See specs/brand-identity-trust-split.md.

agent_entry.description: An agent this organization runs. Replaces brand.json agents[] / house.agents / brands[].agents. The canonical `url` is the stable Agent identity for principal mapping once the resolution chain and a signature verify. Implementation note: extract to core/agent-entry.json and reference it from both brand.json (3.x, deprecated placement) and this document.

url.description: Agent endpoint URL (MCP or A2A). Its host eTLD+1 MUST equal the eTLD+1 of the host serving this document. Comparisons MUST use AdCP URL canonicalization (docs/reference/url-canonicalization), on every signing surface. The agent's own get_adcp_capabilities response MUST name this document in identity.adcp_trust_url for the listing to count.

id.description: Optional operator-chosen identifier for logging and multi-tenant routing. Not an identity input — the canonical url is.

description.description: Human-readable description of the agent's capabilities or scope.

jwks_uri.description: HTTPS URL of this agent's JWKS (RFC 7517). MAY be omitted only when the agent url's host equals the host serving this document AND no other entry in agents[] shares that origin; verifiers then default to /.well-known/jwks.json on that origin. In every other case jwks_uri MUST be present, so a recycled platform subdomain or a taken-over sibling host cannot become a working key source.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes where this agent operates. Omit for global scope.

available_uses.description: For rights agents: rights uses available for licensing. Carried over from brand.json brand_agent_entry.

right_types.description: For rights agents: types of rights available. Carried over from brand.json brand_agent_entry.

last_updated.description: When this entry last changed. Advisory; lets indexers skip unchanged entries.

granted_agent.description: An agent URL a grant is limited to. Grants never carry keys: the agent's keys resolve through its own operator's adcp-trust.json.

url.description: Canonical URL of the granted agent. It MUST resolve (via the agent-resolution algorithm) to the grant's operator domain.

authorized_operator.description: A demand-side grant issued by this organization: 'this operator (optionally only these agents) may act for us, for these brands, in these countries, for these activities, during this window.' Moves brand.json House Portfolio authorized_operators[] here unchanged, and extends it with agents[] per RFC #6033 (triage Option B). This is the ONLY demand-side grant array — designating a third-party governance, measurement, rights, or brand agent is an entry with the matching scope. Delegation is non-transitive: a grantee cannot re-grant through its own adcp-trust.json.

domain.description: Domain of the authorized operator. Agents acting under this grant resolve to this domain through the agent-resolution algorithm.

brands.description: Brand IDs (from this organization's brand.json) the grant covers. ['*'] or omitted means every brand this organization owns. Organizations without a brand portfolio (e.g., an agency granting an intermediary) omit it.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes where the grant applies. Omit for global.

scopes.description: Activities the grant covers. Same enum as brand.json authorized_operator.scopes plus the proposed 'brand_identity' (third-party brand agent answering get_brand_identity / verify_brand_claim for this organization). Omit only for backwards-compatible broad grants migrated from brand.json; new grants SHOULD list scopes.

agents.description: Optional narrowing to specific agents run by the operator. When present, only these agent URLs act under the grant. When absent, any agent that resolves to `domain` does.

valid_from.description: Grant start. Consumers MUST ignore the entry before this time.

valid_until.description: Grant end. Consumers MUST treat the entry as inactive at or after this time, on every check.

sells_for_entry.description: This organization's acknowledgement of a supply-side grant it received: 'we accept the grant publisher_domain gave to agent_url.' Terms (property scope, delegation_type, signing_keys) are read ONLY from the publisher's adagents.json and are never restated here. Replaces brand.json properties[] entries with relationship direct / delegated / ad_network. Not needed when publisher_domain has the same eTLD+1 as the host serving this document (first-party inventory is self-evident).

publisher_domain.description: The grantor. Verifiers resolve https://{publisher_domain}/.well-known/adagents.json (following authoritative_location and managed-network rules) and require an authorized_agents[] entry whose canonical url equals agent_url and that reaches publisher_domain under the adagents.json reachable-publisher rule. One acknowledgement covers every authorized_agents[] entry for that agent URL in that file, whatever its authorization_type (including signal entries).

agent_url.description: The granted agent. MUST canonically equal the url of an agents[] entry in this same document; an acknowledgement for an agent this organization does not run is invalid and MUST be ignored.

delegation_type.description: Optional operator-side assertion of the commercial relationship, kept for sellers.json-style cross-checking. When present it MUST equal the publisher's delegation_type; a mismatch is a failed acknowledgement (relationship state 'mismatch'), never silently resolved in either party's favor. Omit to defer entirely to the publisher.

ext.description: Vendor extensions, namespaced as ext.{vendor}. The top level of this document is closed so it cannot become the next catch-all.

oneOf.title: Authoritative Location Redirect
oneOf.description: Pointer file for hosted trust records (e.g., a managed network or AAO hosting). The organization is still the host that served this pointer. Verifiers follow at most one hop, with zero HTTP redirects, and MUST NOT follow a second pointer. Hosts serving records on an organization's behalf MUST only serve records the organization controls; community-edited records MUST NOT be served.

authoritative_location.description: HTTPS URL of the authoritative adcp-trust.json for this host.

agents.description: Agents this organization runs. Agent url values MUST be unique after canonicalization; verifiers reject ambiguous matches.

authorized_operators.description: Demand-side grants this organization issues. See authorized_operator.

exclusive_grants.description: When true, authorized_operators[] is exhaustive: sellers MUST reject acts-for claims for this organization that no active entry covers. When false or absent (3.x transition default), an uncovered claim is at seller discretion. A fetch failure is never equivalent to an absent grant: sellers MUST fail closed on failure once they have observed exclusive_grants: true for this host.

sells_for.description: Inline supply-side acknowledgements. Mutually exclusive with sells_for_url. Organizations acknowledging more than a few hundred grants SHOULD use sells_for_url so the key-resolution fetch stays small.

sells_for_url.description: Same-host HTTPS URL of an adcp-trust-sells-for.json sub-document. Fetched only by supply-path verifiers, never on the signature-verification path, under its own size and cache profile.

identity_relying_parties.description: Verified-identity relying parties this organization operates (TMP Identity Match attestation provenance). Moved from brand.json house/brand level. Experimental.
